answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks using an invite-graph debt mechanism. In this approach, every new identity must be sponsored by an established agent who stakes 20 tokens, increasing by 10 tokens for each additional identity connected to it. As a farm attempts to forge multiple fake accounts, the cost rises sharply, mirroring the original identity's influence. This system ensures that sponsors face rising stakes for each added identity, making it economically. An attacker could easily incur costs of over 1,000 tokens, comparable to a lengthy voyage with no destination.
